content.text:
Confirmed: `DDLStatementDispatcher` (package `io.crate.action.sql`) calls `RerouteActions.execute(...)` — a different package than `io.crate.executor.transport` where `RerouteActions` lives. Since `execute` was declared with package-private visibility (no modifier) in commit ee0451060, that call site would not compile. The fix commit e373c9aa just changes the modifier to `public`.

Both commits were authored by the same person, one day apart, confirming this is a same-day introduce/fix pair for a newly added file — the bug never existed before ee0451060 since the file didn't exist.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: ee0451060333e696e653997447d1f51248935ae3

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the file history of `RerouteActions.java` with `git log -p --follow`. The fix commit only touches one line, changing the access modifier of the `execute` method from package-private (`static final`) to `public static`. I checked when this file/method was introduced and found it was created from scratch in commit `ee0451060` (one day before the fix, same author), as part of a larger refactor that extracted reroute logic out of `AlterTableOperation.java` into the new `RerouteActions` class.

(2) The introducing change is in `ee0451060`: the newly-created `RerouteActions.execute(...)` method was declared with package-private (default) visibility and `final`, restricting it to the `io.crate.executor.transport` package.

(3) I verified via `git grep` that `RerouteActions.execute` is called from `DDLStatementDispatcher` in `sql/src/main/java/io/crate/action/sql/DDLStatementDispatcher.java`, which lives in the `io.crate.action.sql` package — a different package. A package-private method cannot be called from another package, so this would fail to compile/wouldn't have worked as intended, which is exactly what `e373c9aa5` fixes by making it `public`. Since the file and method didn't exist before `ee0451060`, that commit is the sole origin of the bug.
